episode.title: Why a hydraulic cylinder pushes harder than it pulls
episode.subject: A double-acting hydraulic cylinder, 140 mm bore x 100 mm rod, at 350 bar implement pressure

facts.claim: The implement hydraulic circuit of a 21.7 tonne Caterpillar 320 excavator operates at a normal maximum pressure of 350 bar (35 000 kPa).

evidence.note: Caterpillar's own published specification. The 380 bar Auto Dig Boost figure is transient and is deliberately not used.

facts.claim: For a 140 mm bore and 100 mm rod, the piston area is 153.94 cm2, the rod area is 78.54 cm2 and the annulus area is 75.40 cm2.

evidence.note: All three figures are printed by the manufacturer in the A1, A2 and A3 columns. Independently derived from the geometry this session as 153.94 / 78.54 / 75.40 - agreement to 0.002 cm2.

review.notes: Claim widened 2026-09-18 to carry the rod area, 78.54 cm2, because the restaged Beat 3 puts that number on screen and the previous claim did not cover it - the script hash check caught it. S001 already publishes it in the A2 column, so this is a claim gap, not a sourcing gap. RETURNED TO agent_checked 2026-09-19: the Tier 1 re-edit rewrote the narration (120 words -> 77, and the running order changed). No fact moved; the wording that was signed off did.

facts.claim: The standard piston rod is the bore divided by the square root of two, which puts half the piston's area under the rod and leaves half as the annulus. Rexroth publishes an area-ratio column; the standard series measures 1.96 to 2.08 across the range, so a realised cylinder lands within a point of half rather than exactly on it.

evidence.note: Rexroth prints the area ratio A1/A3 in its own column and offers every bore with two rods; the standard series measures 1.96-2.08, i.e. rod/bore = 0.700-0.720 against 1/sqrt(2) = 0.7071. 'The phi = 2 series' is our shorthand for that column, not a label observed on the document. The spread is rounding to stock rod diameters: 140/sqrt(2) = 99.0 -> 100 mm = 48.98%.
Four of Caterpillar's five 320 boom cylinder variants (120x85, 140x100, 150x105) fall on the same ratio; 160x95 is the slim-rod outlier.

review.notes: Restated 2026-09-18: 'exactly half' and 'manufacturers designate this the phi = 2 series' both overreached. Design intent is half; realised cylinders are within a point. Narration says 'half', never 'exactly half' - the on-screen callout reads 153.94 -> 75.40, which is 48.98%, and a viewer can divide. facts.claim: At 350 bar a 140 x 100 cylinder extends with 538.8 kN (54.9 tonnes-force) and retracts with 263.9 kN (26.9 tonnes-force).

evidence.note: Supplies both areas. Rexroth's own force columns at its 250 bar nominal are 384.75 / 188.40 kN; derived from the same areas this session as 384.85 / 188.50, i.e. the vendor rounds.

review.notes: Force = pressure x area is arithmetic, not a claim needing its own source; both inputs are TIER-1. Replaces the previous draft's unsourced 395.8 / 219.9 kN.
